title: Combine basics: publishers, subscribers, operators
summary: Combine is Apple's reactive framework: a publisher emits values over time, operators transform them, and a subscriber receives them. Still common in existing codebases.
body: **In simple words:** Think of a pipe. Values flow from a **publisher** (search text changes, network response, timer) through **operators** (debounce, map, filter) to a **subscriber** (`sink`, `assign`) that uses them.
**Real-life analogy:** A newspaper subscription. The publisher prints issues, you subscribe, and you keep receiving issues until you cancel.

**Key pieces:** `Just`, `Future`, `URLSession.dataTaskPublisher`, `NotificationCenter.publisher`, `@Published` properties are publishers. `PassthroughSubject` sends values you push manually; `CurrentValueSubject` also remembers the latest value.
**Cancellation and memory:** `sink` returns an `AnyCancellable`. Store it (usually in `Set<AnyCancellable>`); when it is deallocated the subscription stops. Use `[weak self]` inside `sink` closures.
**Threading:** `receive(on: DispatchQueue.main)` before updating UI; `subscribe(on:)` controls where upstream work starts.

**Combine vs async/await today:** new code mostly uses async/await, `AsyncSequence` and Observation. Combine is still great for complex event pipelines (debounce, combineLatest) and is everywhere in apps built 2019-2023. You can bridge with `publisher.values`.
keyPoints: Publisher → operators → subscriber; each subscription is an `AnyCancellable`.
Subjects: `PassthroughSubject` (no current value) vs `CurrentValueSubject` (has current value).
Must store cancellables, or the pipeline stops immediately.
Typical use: search with `debounce`, `removeDuplicates`, `flatMap`/`switchToLatest` to cancel old requests.

mistakes: Strongly capturing `self` in `sink` stored on `self` - retain cycle.
followups: **`map` vs `flatMap` in Combine?** `map` transforms values; `flatMap` turns each value into a new publisher (e.g. a network call) and merges results.
**What is backpressure?** A subscriber controlling how many values it wants (`Demand`); Combine supports it, `sink` requests unlimited.
**`combineLatest` vs `zip`?** combineLatest emits whenever any input changes (using latest of each); zip pairs values one-to-one.
